gloss: be light, shine; give light; light, daylight; fire, flame
summary: The root is light and its shining. אוֹר is the light God called into being on the first day and named “day” (Gen 1:3–5), the light of morning, of sun and moon, and of lightning; then the light of life, of deliverance and joy, of God’s face turned toward a man, and of his word and law that show the way (Psa 27:1; 119:105). The verb is to grow light, and in the hiphil to give light: the luminaries shine on the earth, the lamps of the lampstand give light, Yahweh makes his face shine on his people (Num 6:25). מָאוֹר is a light-giver, the sun and moon or the lampstand’s light; אוּר is fire, the light of flame. Ugaritic ʾr and Punic ʾr “light” and Akkadian urru “daytime” are the same word.

words.gloss: light; daylight, morning; lightning; light of life, of favour, of guidance
words.summary: Light, the opposite of darkness: first the light God made before the sun, then daylight and the light of the heavenly bodies. Its figurative uses all keep that ground: to be alive is to see light, to be favoured is to have the light of a face upon you, to be taught is to have a light on your path.

senses.definition: Light itself, the first thing God spoke into being, divided from darkness and named day; the thing darkness is the absence of.

evidence.note: “Let there be אוֹר”, and there was אוֹר: on the first day, before the sun is made on the fourth (Gen 1:14–19).
God saw the אוֹר, that it was good, and divided between the אוֹר and the חֹשֶׁךְ.
“God called the אוֹר day, and the darkness he called night.”
The luminaries are set to divide between the אוֹר and the darkness.
“Forming אוֹר and creating darkness, making peace and creating evil: I am Yahweh.”
“Where is the way to where the אוֹר dwells, and darkness, where is its place?”
A boundary circled on the waters, to the end of אוֹר with darkness.
The land as before creation: “without form and void; and to the heavens, and their אוֹר was not”.
Wisdom excels folly as אוֹר excels darkness.
Darkness on Egypt three days, but all the sons of Israel had אוֹר in their dwellings.
Yahweh wraps himself in אוֹר as a garment.
“God who said, Out of darkness light shall shine”: Paul quotes the first day.

senses.gloss: daylight, daybreak, the light of morning
senses.definition: The light of day as it breaks: the time a night ends and a man can be seen and act.

evidence.note: They lay in wait all night: “until the אוֹר of the morning, then we will kill him”.
The woman fell at the door of the man’s house “until the אוֹר”.
“Let us plunder them until the אוֹר of the morning.”
David: none of Nabal’s would have been left “by the אוֹר of the morning”.
Abigail told him nothing “until the אוֹר of the morning”.
By the אוֹר of the morning not one was missing who had not crossed the Jordan.
The just ruler is “like the אוֹר of morning when the sun rises, a morning without clouds”.
If we wait until the אוֹר of the morning, punishment will find us.
Ezra read the law “from the אוֹר until midday”: from daybreak.
They devise evil on their beds, and “in the אוֹר of the morning they do it”.
“At אוֹר the murderer rises”: at daybreak.
Those who rebel against the אוֹר: the murderer, the adulterer, the thief, who work in the dark (Job 24:13–16).
One day, not day and not night, and “at evening time there will be אוֹר”.

senses.gloss: light of sun, moon and stars
senses.definition: The light the heavenly bodies give; darkened in judgment, multiplied in restoration.

evidence.note: Yahweh “gives the sun for אוֹר by day, the statutes of the moon and the stars for אוֹר by night”.
The stars will not flash their light; the sun is dark at its rising, and the moon will not make its אוֹר shine.
“The אוֹר of the moon will be as the אוֹר of the sun, and the אוֹר of the sun sevenfold, as the אוֹר of seven days.”
Over Pharaoh: the moon will not give its אוֹר.
“I will make the sun go down at noon, and darken the earth in a day of אוֹר.”
“If I looked at the אוֹר when it shone, or the moon moving in splendour” and my heart was enticed.
“To him who made great אוֹרִים.”
“Praise him, all you stars of אוֹר.”
“The sun shall no longer be your אוֹר by day … but Yahweh will be to you an everlasting אוֹר.”
Before the sun and the אוֹר and the moon and the stars are darkened.

senses.definition: The light flashed from the storm cloud, which God spreads, covers and sends.

evidence.note: “Under the whole heavens he lets it go, and his אוֹר to the ends of the earth”, with his thunder (37:2–4).
“He scatters the cloud of his אוֹר.”
“Do you know … how he makes the אוֹר of his cloud to flash?”
He spreads his אוֹר about him.
“He covers his hands with אוֹר, and commands it to strike the mark.”
Sun and moon stood still at the אוֹר of your arrows, at the flash of your glittering spear.

senses.gloss: light of life; to see light, to be alive
senses.definition: To see light is to be alive in the world; the dead and the stillborn do not see it, and one brought back from the pit is lit again with the light of the living.

evidence.note: “As a hidden stillbirth I would not be, as infants who never saw אוֹר.”
“Why is אוֹר given to the wretched, and life to the bitter of soul?”: אוֹר set beside חַיִּים.
He shall go to the generation of his fathers; “to eternity they will not see אוֹר”.
“You delivered my soul from death … to walk before God in the אוֹר of the living.”
“He redeemed my soul from going down to the pit, and my life will see the אוֹר.”
To bring back his soul from the pit, to be lit with the אוֹר of the living.
“The אוֹר of the wicked goes out”: his life and house come to nothing (18:5–21).
“He is driven from אוֹר into darkness, and chased out of the world.”
“The אוֹר of my eyes, even that is not with me”: strength failing.
“Sweet is the אוֹר, and good for the eyes to see the sun”, set against the many days of darkness (11:8).

senses.gloss: light of deliverance, prosperity and joy
senses.definition: Good that comes after trouble: rescue, gladness, a righteous man’s vindication; darkness is its opposite, calamity and judgment.

Matthew quotes Isa 9:1 of Jesus beginning to preach in Galilee.
“I hoped for good, and evil came; I waited for אוֹר, and darkness came.”
The day of Yahweh is “darkness and not אוֹר” to those who desire it (and 5:20).
“We wait for אוֹר, and behold darkness”, beside “justice is far from us”.
“He has led me and made me walk in darkness and not אוֹר.”
“אוֹר is sown for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart.”
“אוֹר rises in the darkness for the upright.”
“When I sit in darkness, Yahweh is a אוֹר to me”; 7:9, he will bring me out to the אוֹר.
“Then your אוֹר will break forth like the dawn, and your healing spring up quickly.”
The אוֹר of the righteous rejoices, but the lamp of the wicked goes out.
The path of the righteous is like the אוֹר of dawn, shining more and more to the full day.
“אוֹר will shine on your ways.”

senses.definition: The light of a face turned toward someone: the favour of God or of a king, on which life and good depend.

evidence.note: “Many say, Who will show us good? Lift up the אוֹר of your face upon us, Yahweh.”
“In the אוֹר of the king’s face is life, and his favour is like a cloud of the latter rain.”
Not their own arm saved them, “but your right hand and your arm and the אוֹר of your face, because you favoured them”.
“Blessed the people … Yahweh, they walk in the אוֹר of your face.”
Job: “the אוֹר of my face they did not cast down”.

senses.gloss: light that guides: Yahweh, his word, his law and his servant
senses.definition: Light to walk by: Yahweh himself, and the word, law and judgment he sends to lead men, and the servant he gives as a light to the nations.

evidence.note: “Yahweh is my אוֹר and my salvation; whom shall I fear?”
“Your word is a lamp to my feet and a אוֹר to my path.”
“The commandment is a lamp and the law a אוֹר, and the reproofs of instruction the way of life.”
“Send your אוֹר and your truth; let them lead me, let them bring me to your holy hill.”
“With you is the fountain of life; in your אוֹר we see אוֹר.”
“House of Jacob, come and let us walk in the אוֹר of Yahweh”, after the law goes out from Zion (2:3).
“A law will go out from me, and my justice for a אוֹר of the peoples.”
“Your judgments go forth as אוֹר.”
Morning by morning Yahweh brings his justice to אוֹר.
“When his lamp shone over my head, by his אוֹר I walked through darkness.”
The servant given “for a covenant of the people, for a אוֹר of the nations, to open blind eyes”.
“I will give you for a אוֹר of the nations, to be my salvation to the end of the earth.” Quoted at Acts 13:47.
Simeon of the child Jesus: “a light for revelation to the nations”.
Paul and Barnabas quote Isa 49:6 as the command under which they turn to the nations.
That the Christ, first to rise from the dead, would proclaim light to the people and to the nations.
“Arise, shine, for your אוֹר has come, and the glory of Yahweh has risen upon you”; nations come to it (60:3).
“Yahweh will be your everlasting אוֹר, and the days of your mourning will be ended.”
“The אוֹר of Israel will become a fire, and his Holy One a flame”: the same light that guides Israel burns its enemy.

words.summary: The verb of the noun: of day, to grow light; of eyes, to brighten; and in the hiphil, to give light or make something shine. Its commonest figure is Yahweh making his face shine on his people, from the priests’ blessing (Num 6:25) through the Psalms.

senses.definition: Of the day, to grow light at dawn.

“Rise early in the morning, and when it is light for you, go.”

senses.definition: To give out light: Zion when Yahweh’s glory has risen on her, and the path of the righteous.

evidence.note: קוּמִי אוֹרִי, “arise, shine, for your light has come”.
The path of the righteous, “going on and shining (וָאוֹר) until the full day”.
“Awake, sleeper, and arise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you”: the call of Isa 60:1 (and 26:19) to the believer.

senses.definition: Of a faint man’s eyes, to brighten as strength returns.

“See how my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.”

senses.definition: To be shining, or to be lit with light.

evidence.note: “Radiant (נָאוֹר) are you, majestic, from the mountains of prey.”
To bring back his soul from the pit, “to be lit (לֵאוֹר) with the light of the living”.

By night a pillar of fire “to give them light”, to go by day and night.

To you the night shines as the day.

senses.definition: Of Yahweh, to make his face shine on someone: to turn toward them in favour, to be gracious and save.

The blessing of Num 6:25 prayed for, so that his way be known among the nations (67:3).

“Make your face shine on your sanctuary that is desolate.”
A man’s wisdom makes his face shine.

“The opening of your words gives light, giving understanding to the simple.”

words.gloss: light-giver, luminary; the light (of the lampstand)
words.summary: A place or bearer of light, formed with the prefix ma-: the sun and moon set in the expanse to give light, and in the sanctuary the light of the lampstand, for which the oil was brought.

“Let them be for מְאוֹרֹת … to give light on the earth.”
“The two great מְאֹרֹת, the great מָאוֹר to rule the day and the small מָאוֹר to rule the night.”
“Yours is the day, yours also the night; you established מָאוֹר and sun.”
“All the מְאוֹרֵי אוֹר in the heavens I will darken over you.”

The same command for the oil, “for the מָאוֹר, to make a lamp go up continually” (Lev 24:1–4).
“Oil for the מָאֹר.”
“The lampstand of the מָאוֹר … and the oil of the מָאוֹר.”
“The lampstand of the מָאוֹר, and its lamps.”
Eleazar’s charge: “the oil of the מָאוֹר”.

“The מְאוֹר of the eyes rejoices the heart.”

words.gloss: fire, flame; (pl. אֻרִים) the regions of light, the east
words.summary: Fire seen as light: the blaze a man warms himself at and walks by. Rare (about six times, all in the prophets), and set beside אֵשׁ, “fire”. Its tie to the root is the light of flame. The plural בָּאֻרִים (Isa 24:15), set against “the coastlands of the sea”, is read as the regions of light, the east; that reading rests on one verse. No cognate checked here shares the sense “fire” (Arabic uwār “blaze” is a lead not yet checked), so the count of cognates runs against it; its tie to the root rests on the verses’ light of flame.

senses.gloss: fire, flame, the light of a fire
senses.definition: A fire, as something that gives light and warmth.

The fire burns Babylon’s counsellors: “no coal to warm by, no אוּר to sit before”.
“Walk in the אוּר of your fire and in the sparks you have kindled.”
Yahweh, “whose אוּר is in Zion, and his furnace in Jerusalem”.
A third of the hair burned “in the אוּר in the midst of the city”.

senses.definition: In Isa 24:15, the plural set against “the coastlands of the sea” (the west): the lands where light rises. One verse only.

words.gloss: the Urim (of the high priest’s breastpiece)
words.summary: Five times paired with the Thummim, “wholenesses”, and twice alone (Num 27:21; 1Sa 28:6): the things put in the breastpiece of judgment, by which judgment was asked of Yahweh. In form it is the plural of אוּר, “lights” or “fires”, but scripture never says why it is so named, nor what the Urim were, so its tie to the root’s meaning rests on its form alone. No cognate shares it.

senses.definition: Put in the breastpiece of judgment over Aaron’s heart, with the Thummim, so that he bore the judgment of Israel before Yahweh; through them the priest asked Yahweh’s judgment for the leader of the people.

Joshua “shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall ask for him by the judgment of the אוּרִים before Yahweh; at his word they shall go out and come in”.
Saul asked of Yahweh, and Yahweh did not answer him, “neither by dreams, nor by אוּרִים, nor by prophets”: one of the ways Yahweh answered.
Moses put the אוּרִים and תֻּמִּים in the breastpiece at Aaron’s consecration.
Of Levi: “Your Thummim and your Urim are with your godly one.”
Priests without a record of descent may not eat the most holy things “until a priest stands up with אוּרִים and תֻּמִּים”: none was then at hand.

cognates.note: Akkadian urru is the day as against the night, in Middle and Neo-Assyrian and later texts. Hebrew אוֹר is named “day” at its making (Gen 1:5) and is daybreak in narrative (Neh 8:3; Job 24:14). Akkadian’s ordinary word for light, nūru, is of another root (נור).

doctrine.statement: On the first day God said “let there be אוֹר”, divided it from the darkness and called it day, and evening and morning were one day (Gen 1:3–5); the sun, moon and stars, the מְאֹרֹת, were made on the fourth day to give light on the earth and to mark days and years (Gen 1:14–19). Yahweh says he forms light and creates darkness (Isa 45:7), and Psa 74:16 sets the day, the night, the luminary and the sun all as his. From the verses: light is a thing God made by his word, on a day of evening and morning, before the bodies that now carry it. Paul takes that first word as the pattern of what God does in believers: the God who said “out of darkness light shall shine” has shone in our hearts with the knowledge of his glory in the face of Jesus Christ (2Co 4:6).

Yahweh is Israel’s light and salvation (Psa 27:1), and his word and law are a light for the path (Psa 119:105; Pro 6:23). He gives his servant “for a covenant of the people, for a light of the nations” (Isa 42:6), “to be my salvation to the end of the earth” (Isa 49:6). Simeon names the child Jesus “a light for revelation to the nations” (Luk 2:32); Matthew finds the great light of Isa 9:1 in Jesus’ preaching in Galilee (Mat 4:16); Jesus says “I am the light of the world” (Joh 8:12); and Paul, preaching him, applies Isa 49:6 to himself and Barnabas (Act 13:47) and says the Christ, first to rise from the dead, would proclaim light to Israel and the nations (Act 26:23). From the verses: the light is Yahweh’s, given through his servant, the son he raised from the dead, and carried on by those who preach him, who are themselves to shine as luminaries in the world (Php 2:15).

The priests put Yahweh’s name on Israel with the words “Yahweh make his face shine on you and be gracious to you” (Num 6:25, 27). The Psalms pray it back: “make your face shine and we shall be saved” (Psa 80:4, 8, 20), and set the light of his face as the cause of Israel’s victories, “because you favoured them” (Psa 44:4). Paul writes that the light of the knowledge of the glory of God is given in the face of Jesus Christ (2Co 4:6). From the verses: the shining face is favour turned toward a people, and its fruit is grace and salvation; in the New Testament God’s favour is seen in Christ.

To see light, in scripture’s idiom, is to be alive: the stillborn “never saw light” (Job 3:16), and light is given with life (Job 3:20). The man who dies goes to the generation of his fathers, and “to eternity they will not see light” (Psa 49:20); he is like the beasts that perish. Deliverance from death is to walk “in the light of the living” (Psa 56:14), and God’s redeeming a soul from the pit is that it is lit again “with the light of the living” (Job 33:28, 30). From the verses: death is darkness, not a passing into another light; light is had again only by being brought back from the pit by God.

Isaiah sees Zion told “arise, shine, for your light has come”, nations coming to its light, and the sun and moon no longer its light because Yahweh will be its everlasting light (Isa 60:1–3, 19–20); in that day the light of the moon will be as the sun’s, and the sun’s sevenfold (Isa 30:26), and Zechariah says at evening there will be light (Zec 14:7). John’s holy city has no need of sun or moon, for the glory of God lights it and the Lamb is its lamp, and the nations walk in its light (Rev 21:23–24; 22:5). From the verses: the light promised to Zion is Yahweh’s own presence among his people, and the nations come to it on the earth.
